name: Console commands help
description: Help mode entries for the Console commands plugin (help@1): its settings tab, the open consoles list, the last commands, and seeing and driving the console by voice.
author: Brett

entries.title: Console commands settings
entries.text: Lets a Claude session (Amber), the REST API or the CLI open screens, dialogs and settings tabs in this console, run its actions and go back. Opening only moves the screen; an action that changes data still needs its own permission, and one that deletes or resets needs a confirm.

entries.title: Let Claude sessions move this console
entries.text: On: this console listens for console commands and goes where they say. Off: it stops listening, and commands go to your other open consoles.

entries.title: Show a note for each command
entries.text: Shows a short note each time a command moves this console, saying who asked and what opened.

entries.title: Refresh
entries.text: Reloads the list of open consoles and the last commands from the console server.

entries.title: Let Claude sessions move this console
entries.text: On: this console listens for console commands and goes where they say. Off: it stops listening, and commands go to your other open consoles.

entries.title: Show a note for each command
entries.text: Shows a short note each time a command moves this console, saying who asked and what opened.

entries.title: Wake the console through AmberX when it's closed
entries.text: On: a console command that finds no open console waits on the server, and after a few seconds AmberX on your phone opens the console so the command runs. Off: the command waits for you to open a console yourself.

entries.title: How long a command waits for a console
entries.text: How long a waiting command stays in the queue. After this it is dropped, so a command never runs late.

entries.title: Browser AmberX opens
entries.text: Which browser AmberX uses when it wakes the console: Chrome, or the phone's default browser.

entries.title: Seeing and driving the console on a voice call
entries.text: On a voice call a picture never reaches Amber, so console_screenshot also answers in words: a literal description of the screen and a numbered list of everything that can be pressed, with where each one is. Say "click Retry", "right-click that row", "expand row 3", "open the app menu, go to Settings" or "jump to the queue" and Amber does it, then tells you what the screen shows now.
entries.more: The description covers headings, tabs, buttons, rows with their text and status, banners, errors, dialogs, open menus and numbers, with no guessing. The tools: console_click, console_right_click, console_double_click, console_context_menu, console_menu, console_expand, console_collapse, console_jump, console_scroll, console_type and console_key. Each takes words (a transcription slip still matches), a number from the list, a console-control address or x,y on the screenshot.

entries.title: What Amber will not press by voice
entries.text: When several things match your words Amber gets the numbered choices and asks which one; she never guesses. A control that deletes, stops or merges is only pressed after she told you what it will do and sent the call again with confirm. Approve and deny are never pressed by a command: they stay your own tap.
entries.more: A click that can change data waits for the usual veto unless a pass is on; right-click, expand, collapse, scroll and jump run at once.

entries.title: Who describes the screenshot
entries.text: The console server sends the PNG to Claude through the AI assistant's own providers (the Anthropic key set up in Settings › Plugins › AI assistant; no other route), Opus by default. One description is one model call, counted in the AI assistant's usage.
entries.more: The model is describeModel in this plugin's server settings: claude-opus-5-5 or claude-fable-5-2. It gives up after 30 seconds (the list and the image still come, with a note) and the same unchanged screen is not described again for 2 minutes.
